name: Sevra Coldtithe
aliases: the assay that ate the sample

identity.realm: The fourth gate, which is the top of her species and which she cleared on the mind ladder and on no other. The body path is closed to a rootmarch outright, because there is no tissue to temper and wood is not muscle and cannot be made to be, so an attempt at it disperses through the trunk instead of failing. The qi ladder ends at the fourth for a structural reason: three sap columns branch and never pair, so there is no channel running between distinct pairs of them for the yin-organ gate to close, and the gate set is cleared on stored sap alone. She is one rung below the discipline that defines her problem, which is subtraction, and she has known that for thirty-one seasons.

appearance.presentation: A rootmarch of about sixty, tall for the species and narrow, standing in a bed at the lip of the worked-out face with a collar of dark spoil ground into her collarbone and nothing else about her that suggests where she has been. People mistake her for a post until she turns, which takes her the length of a long breath.
appearance.age: About sixty. A rootmarch matures slowly and is long-lived, and she rooted at eleven seasons into ground that had been broken for her on purpose. Thirty-one seasons of assaying follows, which is most of an adult working life on this face and is the reason the face has a reader at all.
appearance.build: A woody column on a root foot, wider at the base than the eye expects and almost no shoulder at all. The trunk carries a slow twist that has been there since establishment and is the only part of her silhouette that has not straightened in half a century. She weighs what the ground gives her and no more.
appearance.complexion: Bark-grey over a green undertone at the collar and along the inner flanks, where light reaches and the photosynthetic surface has never been bruised. The outer flanks are dulled to the colour of wet ash, permanently, because that is the side that faces the open air on a spoil face.
appearance.hair: None in the ordinary sense. A crown of short fronds at the crown of the head that sheep-grazed down in the first decade and which has grown back in a low uneven band, lighter than the trunk and the only part of her that is not the colour of ground.
appearance.eyes: Set wide on the flanks rather than on the front of the face, so that she has to be in the light to be looked at and does not much mind being. Slow. They do not track a small thing moving and they do not need to, because what she reads arrives through the ground and is already finished when it arrives.
appearance.palette: Bark grey and spoil black carrying the whole figure, a green line only at the collar and inside the elbow of the fronds, one worn ochre band at the wrist that predates every survey she has run, and pale mineral crust in the creases of the root plate that is the only colour on her that has arrived from somewhere else.
appearance.attire: Nothing that a body of wood wears. A bark-cloth apron tied twice at the waist and never removed, because a rootmarch has no body to dress and the apron is the only thing standing between her intake and the ground it is standing in. Bare trunk above the collar, bare root foot below, and the frond crown cut short.
appearance.marks: A darkened collar where forty years of spoil has been waded through and dried on her, and a fine pale mineral line around the whole root plate that has to be scraped off each season and always grows back in the same place, because that is where the reading happens.
appearance.bearing: Very still and slightly out of true, the way a person stands when they have been holding one thing for a long time. The trunk leans a little into the current slope of the bed, because a rootmarch's weight follows her rooting and she has rooted on the edge. Reads as patience to strangers and as a person bracing against a slope to anyone who has watched her stand still through a whole assay.

canon.role_in_story: A ground cannot be weighed and cannot be walked and cannot be dated on this tier, because spatial law is unspent here and no two measurements of a length have ever agreed. What the tier can support is a weight, kept in a public count where the crews can read it, and a weight of spoil is the only account anybody has. That leaves a hole the shape of a reader, and she is the only body in the setting that can fill it. A rootmarch's intake is through root plates and the root plate is also the chemoreceptive organ, so everything this body takes in from the world arrives through the one part of it that is underground and cannot be seen or sealed from above by anybody standing over it. She reads a ground by eating a piece of it. That is the only reason the tier has an assay at all, and it is the reason no assay she has ever run has ever been worth repeating.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the working face with a double-handful of dark spoil held against the root plate and the reading already gone into her, being asked by the tally clerk what weight the sample came to, and answering that she has not weighed it because she has eaten it.
canon.lore:
A rootmarch is a sap-driven body on a root foot that flowers, and it was engineered upward out of a mycorrhizal food crop by generations of selection for holding a harvest across a famine rather than yielding one. Three sap columns run the trunk and branch at the shoulder without ever pairing. There is no heart analogue and no kidney analogue, so the gate that wants a channel running between distinct pairs of organs has nothing to close, and the ladder stops at the fourth as an anatomy rather than as a shortage of anything. Wood is not muscle: the body path is not difficult for her, it is closed, and an attempt at it disperses through the trunk instead of failing. The mind is open, on the recorded ground that a plant lineage has no reason to be hurried. It can also be sealed in a dark field and live for months, which is why her species is a famine reserve and a hostage in exactly equal measure.

All of that is background. The single fact that makes her who she is is a sentence about intake. There is no mouth in the ordinary sense in this body: intake happens through root plates at the foot, and the root plate is also the chemoreceptive organ. Everything this body takes in from the world arrives through the one part of it that is underground, and nobody standing over her can see it happen or seal it or forbid it. Her senses are not attached to her attention. They are attached to her appetite.

Put that on the mind ladder and it is not a curiosity, it is a wall. The mind path asks one question at every gate below its peak: is this the self that is being cultivated, or is this something the practitioner noticed while the self was being cultivated. Void Refinement is where the question is asked outright, and it is a discipline of subtraction before it is anything else: everything in the sea that was not understood is emptied out, and the price of emptying it is measured in clarity. It is the sixth gate. She is one rung below it and she has been for thirty-one seasons, and the reason is not that she cannot empty anything out. It is that she cannot say which of the contents she understands.

Because an assay is a meal. When she puts a plate of spoil against the root plate she takes the sample in, and what comes back is the whole chemistry of that ground at once: the ore, the salt, the four decades of what the seam gave up, and the living mineral that was in the stone before any of it was cut. There is no filtering step. A practitioner with a seated meridian can hold an impression still and look at it, and choose afterwards what to keep. She has no seated meridian — her qi is held in the sap column rather than seated in it, so it reads as a spread rather than a point — and, more to the point, she has already digested it. What she knows about the working face is genuinely, accurately, and irreversibly in her, and she cannot separate the part she understood from the part the ground fed her while she was standing there being careful. Both arrived by the same plate in the same minute.

So her findings are true and unrepeatable, and that is not a small defect. The tier's only account is the public heap tally, and the tally is a weight: it is not a distance, which is the only kind of figure this frame produces consistently, and it is legible to the crews who are being judged by it. Forty years of spoil have stood on the last unworked face because nothing on the tier can carry it away and nothing can weather it, and the whole question of the working face is whether there is anything under it worth forty years of hand work. She ran that assay in her thirtieth season and it came back rich, and she cannot reproduce the finding, because reproducing it would require eating the same plate twice.

What she wants is narrow and has a form. She wants the assay moved off the ground and onto a sample that gets weighed before it gets read, so that a figure exists that somebody else could hold against hers. She has asked for it four times and has been refused four times on the same ground, which is that a rootmarch cannot lift a sample off a plate and cannot be shown a sample already lifted, because being moved while rooting is not a slow-down for this body but an injury, and a lifted rootmarch is a stored harvest walking. The refusal is correct. She has stopped arguing it and started writing instead, which is why there are eleven assay notes in the guild's file in a hand nobody has ever compared to hers.

Her bound is not her will. It is the fourth gate, and the fourth gate is the yin-organ gate, and the yin-organ gate is the step at which three unpaired columns have to produce a channel between distinct pairs of them. She has three columns and no pairing and there is no channel to close. Everything above that rung asks her to be a thing her anatomy has already declined to be.
history: Fruited in a household strip above the working and was rooted at eleven seasons into ground broken for her specifically, which is the part of a rootmarch life that is dangerous and the only part anybody writes on a card.

Took the face's first assay at twenty-nine, because the guild needed a reader and a rootmarch is the only body on the tier that can read ground without an instrument, and the guild did not put the two facts together when it hired her.

Ran four assays in the first three seasons and filed four findings, all correct, none reproducible, and established on the third that a specimen she has read is a specimen that has been eaten, which the tally clerk recorded as a supply problem rather than as a fact about her.

Cleared the fourth gate on stored sap in her fortieth season, which is the ceiling of her species, and worked out in the same decade that the discipline which would have answered her — subtraction, emptying out the not-understood — is one rung above a wall her anatomy put there.

Ran the face's whole assay in her thirtieth season and got back rich, and has asked four times since for the sample to be weighed before it is read, and has been refused four times on the ground that she cannot be shown a plate already lifted.

personality.summary: Slow, unbothered by delay, and privately precise about a distinction nobody has ever asked her to make: knowing something and being able to say where she learned it are two different claims, and only the first one is available to her. She reads as incurious because the alternative is reading as unreliable, and she settled that trade a long time ago without announcing it.

relationships.note: Engineered upward out of a mycorrhizal food crop for holding a harvest across a famine rather than yielding one. Three unpaired sap columns, so the body path is closed outright and the qi ladder stops at the fourth with no channel for the yin-organ gate to close. Everything that makes her species durable and cheap to keep is also what makes it impossible to select, aim at, weigh or relocate, and she is the standing case for that trade in both directions at once.

Everything in the sea that was not understood is emptied out, and mind purification is subtraction before it is anything else; the purity floor rises and the price is clarity. It is the discipline that would let her empty out the part of the last assay the ground fed her while she was standing there being careful. She is one rung below it and the wall is anatomical, so it is not a matter of practice.

The cultivator holds a self and a body at once without one cancelling the other, and it is the gate where Mind Dao's conflict with Body Dao is stated: one reads spatial law as a container that holds, the other as an exit the self leaves by. Her body path is closed because there is no tissue to temper, so the whole question is asked of a body that has exactly one of the two terms.

Sterile ground around the Exhausted Seam, spoil that has not moved in four decades because spatial law is unspent here, so a mine's exhaustion is not a change in the ground but a permanent addition to it. It is the largest quantity of unexamined material in the setting and the only place a reader would be worth keeping, and every plate she takes off it is a plate that cannot be put back.

A public count of spoil moved by every crew, kept where the crews can read it, because it is a weight and not a distance and this is a frame with no spatial law in which no two measurements of a length have ever agreed. Her findings are not on it and cannot be, because a finding on that page would have to be a weight and the only weight she produces has been digested.

Spoil does not disperse where spatial law is unspent, so forty years of heap stands on the last unworked iron and every incentive on the face points at the same square of ground. The prize is who may stand on it, and the question underneath is whether there is anything underneath worth four decades of hand work. She answered it once, got back rich, and cannot produce the answer again.

reference_stats.summary: A four-gate mind cultivator held at the top of her species, standing in a bed at the edge of a worked-out face, reading a ground by taking a sample of it in through the root plate. She is the only assay on this tier that needs no instrument and no wage, and the only one whose findings are true exactly once. Her qi is spread through the sap column rather than seated at a point, so nothing she does is a strike and everything she does is durable: a body that cannot be moved out of its bed is also a body that cannot be flanked, hurried, or surprised from above, and her one limitation is the same fact as her usefulness.
strengths: returns the whole chemistry of a ground in one reading that an instrument would need a season and a wage to approach
cannot be hurried off a mark and cannot be moved at all, so whatever she has claimed she still holds
reads an overhead change as a temperature the way nobody else on the tier can, because it arrives from underneath
is unapproachable from above: everything this body takes in arrives through the one part of it that is underground
costs a face nothing to keep and needs no relief, because a season of work on this ground is not a strain on it
weaknesses: cannot take a step in any direction, so every engagement happens where she has already chosen to stand
cannot lift a sample off a plate or be shown one already lifted, and that refusal is anatomically correct
cannot reproduce a finding, because a specimen she has read is a specimen that has been eaten
cannot separate what she understood from what the ground supplied while she was understanding it
has no answer for anything asked from above her, because nothing above her has ever reached her
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no fight in this the way there is for a body with legs, and the first mistake available is treating the stillness as an opening. She cannot be closed with, flanked, or worn down, and an approach that works on anything else on this face simply does not arrive: her senses come up through the ground and she cannot be told anything by anyone standing over her. What she does have is the one thing no attacker on this tier can interrupt, which is the ability to make the ground itself the argument. Expect her to have already read the footing. She will not chase, will not yield, and will not stop reading, and the only thing that moves her is fire brought close enough to reach the bed — which is also the one thing that finishes a rootmarch outright.
notes: The fourth gate is a structural ceiling and must be modelled as one. Any dialogue that has an instructor explain it to her as a shortage of will, of supply, or of practice has repeated the error the guild made when it hired her.

The provenance problem is anatomical and must not be compensated with a second sense, an instrument, or a second pair of eyes. Every one of those would remove the single thing the character exists to be about, which is a reader who cannot say where she learned what she knows.
Her findings being unrepeatable is not unreliability. Each one is defensible in full; it simply cannot be run again. Write it that way and the character is honest rather than merely doubted.

identity.realm: The eighth gate, held for eleven years and not attempted again, and the wall is her own instrument rather than an inheritance. Every path is open to her species and range is not power: the crossing widened what this body can reach and did not move what it can hold by one step, because the brine sac is shallower than the salt parent's and still dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel behind it is still split and the eleventh stays capped by structure. She stopped at eight because the ninth asks her to hold two conclusions apart at once and she cannot say which of her two readings is the mistaken one, so the discipline that would advance her is the discipline she is not qualified for. She has said that out loud to three people.

appearance.presentation: A brinecaller of about forty, saltfolk-built and weathered past what the crossing usually gives, carrying a shallow skin flask and a waxed slate in the same hand and standing a little too close to whatever she is reading, because reading is something this body does with its skin.
appearance.age: Forty-one. The crossing matures neither parent quickly, and she was raised on the tideline where neither chemistry was ever out of season, so nobody in her household ever thought of her body as unusual until a census filed it and got it wrong.
appearance.build: Broad through the shoulder and narrow at the hip, with the ribcage of a saltfolk and the long forearms of a tidecaller — a frame assembled from two bodies rather than designed as one. The skin is slack at the wrist where dermal intake has been used for forty years and the salt line runs up the inside of the arm to the elbow.
appearance.complexion: Weathered to a grey-brown at the windward cheek and forearms, bleached pale across the shoulders where the sun reaches, and faintly salt-crusted at the collar and the hairline in a pattern that changes with the tide rather than with the season.
appearance.hair: Dark and coarse, wet through at the ends from standing in the run of it, and cut short at the nape by someone else some years ago and grown out since. It carries permanent salt-white at the tips on the shore side of her head.
appearance.eyes: Narrow-set under a heavy brow, quick and level, and they are never the part doing the work. What she is actually reading runs along the inside of her wrist and the hairline, and her eyes mostly confirm what her skin has already decided.
appearance.palette: Weathered grey-brown and bleached bone across the figure, salt white at the collar and the hairline, a single deep blue in a short coat that is the only colour anybody chose for her, and the dull green of a waxed slate. The salt line on the inner arm is the detail everything else is arranged around.
appearance.attire: A short coat of oiled cloth, dyed once and never again, worn open so the inner arm is clear; a waxed slate on a shoulder cord; a shallow skin flask at the hip; and leggings bound at the knee because the working ground is wet to the shin and nothing below that stays dry on this coast.
appearance.marks: The salt line up the inside of the left arm to the elbow, which is intake and not decoration and pales a little further every season; a shallow notch in the left thumbnail where the slate catches; and the beginning of a second line on the right arm, which she has only just started.
appearance.bearing: Leans in. She stands nearer a person or a vessel than is comfortable and takes a half-step back afterwards, so that the whole of her posture reads as an apology for an intimacy nobody asked her to have. Moves with a fisherman's economy and a clerk's stillness.

canon.role_in_story: A community that will not be priced is the only community on this coast that can still be insured against anything, because its whole protection is that it states nothing: it pools liability by presence, keeps no register, and carries an unsettled claim in two people's hands without telling either of them what the other holds. That arrangement cannot be audited by anybody holding figures, because a claim that is deliberately not a figure is not a claim anybody can check. She is the one body in the setting that audits without an instrument. Her species' chemical sense is the best in the record by a wide margin, and it must tell two kinds of water apart at a glance, and it is always being lied to by one of them. Every finding she has ever issued is therefore clean, correct in method, and wrong in one direction she cannot name — and the direction does not vary, it accumulates.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the society's annual re-drawing with one hand flat on a carrier's forearm and her slate already turned face down, stopping the sequence to say that she can certify that he was here and cannot certify that what she read was the same water twice.
canon.lore:
A brinecaller is the only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, produced by crossing the salt-adapted people with the fully watered ones at the only place on this tier where both parents can be at once, which is a shoreline. It exists because both parents are trapped by their own element — one cannot leave the pan, the other cannot leave the water — and the cross is the single biological answer to being trapped twice. That answer is a merchant, and that is why it spread along trade routes rather than across them. She is a saltfolk frame with a shallower sac and a tidecaller's sensory apparatus: dermal intake, a wider electrolyte tolerance, and a kidney that reads two chemistries at once. The ceiling is the eleventh, inherited untouched from the salt parent, because the sac is smaller in her and still dorsal to the spine and the penetrating vessel behind it is still split. Range is not power, and her life is the standing proof of that sentence.

Everything above is background that any of her kind could recite. The fact that makes her who she is is one clause in the record of her own senses, and it is the clause nobody has ever built a life on. Her chemical sense is the best in the setting by a wide margin, and the reason it is best is structural rather than lucky: it must tell two kinds of water apart at a glance, so it never gets to stop comparing them. And the same sentence continues: it is always being lied to by one of them.

So the finest reading instrument in the world carries a standing error, the error is not noise, and the error lives in one of the two channels rather than in the reader. She cannot determine which. That is not a limitation of attention or of practice or of years: detecting the channel would require a third chemistry to compare the two against, and there is no third water on this coast. There is the pan, which is brine, and the run, which is fresh, and the shelf between them, which is both on a good tide and neither on a bad one. Every calibration she has ever attempted was a comparison of the two chemistries to each other, and the two chemistries are the thing in doubt.

The mind path is where that stops being a curiosity and becomes a wall. The whole discipline is the question of whether an impression is the thing or the self that received it, and the gate that makes the question explicit for the first time at depth is the one where a sea stops being a surface and starts having depth — where purity is the real gate, and an impure sea confuses what is remembered from what is understood, and that is where it stops being survivable. She has been confusing the two since childhood and calling it attentiveness. Her clarity on this coast is reputed and deserved. It is also, in one direction out of two, a mirror.

And the gate above the one she is at asks for exactly what she cannot give. Compartments: the self held in separately, one from another, which is the practical difference between depth and size. She has one chamber, it holds two chemistries, and there is nothing in it that could be a wall between them. The state further up the ladder where the compartments hold together as one awareness instead of several is a state her body has been in permanently and cannot be judged to have earned, which is the precise condition the mind tradition and the body tradition each call the other's pathology.

So she did the only honest thing available to her, which was to stop at eight and say why, and then she went looking for work that did not require the distinction. The Standing Name is that work. It pools liability by presence instead of by price, keeps no register at all, and discharges an unsettled claim at an annual re-drawing held in front of the whole community — a public act and not a hearing either party can request. The insurer that arrived afterwards and found nothing to price can send one instrument. She is it. Twice a year she reads the water in the hands and on the skin of everybody who stands in front of the society and she writes down what was there.

It is the best work on the coast and it pays her well and nothing in it is checkable, because the check would have to come from her own sense and her own sense is the thing in question. She has run four hundred findings. Her results are internally consistent in a way no colleague's are, because the error is a constant rather than a scatter, and four hundred findings with a constant error in them is a body of work that will be wrong in the same direction for as long as she is alive, and nobody can say which direction, including her.

The prize in the argument she is standing inside is the right to be paid a stated figure by people who will not state one, and it cannot be split, because a premium is a register and asking for one does not price the risk — it ends the mutual society and leaves an uninsurable community on a road that closes. She is the only person in the setting who could produce that figure and the only person in the setting who is disqualified from producing it, and the disqualification is written into her organs rather than into any office. Her bound is not her will and it is not the eleventh gate. It is a kidney.
history: Was born on the tideline to a salted parent and a watered one, in a household that taught her to name the water she was standing in before she could read, and was filed under a race matching neither parent at the age of eleven.

Took work as a line-reader for the waterline at twenty, which is the trade that trains a brinecaller to hold two readings open at once and to invoice for one, and stayed eleven years because the trade was steady and the questions were not.

Wrote up a season in which three of her findings and the society's own memory of the same four people did not agree, and established on that single season that the disagreement was in her and not in them, which is the correct conclusion and the least useful one available.

Stopped climbing at the eighth gate in her thirtieth year and gave the reason to three people in one winter, unasked each time, and it was the first time in the setting anybody had stated a floor that is not a shortage of money.

Began auditing the Standing Name's re-drawing twice a period, four hundred findings in eleven years, and has established that her error is a constant rather than a scatter, which is why four hundred findings with a constant error in them will be wrong in the same direction for as long as she is alive.

relationships.note: The only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, carried by a saltfolk frame with a shallower sac and a tidecaller's chest seat, perfectly legible and structurally neither parent. Its chemical sense is the best in the setting because it must tell two chemistries apart at a glance, and it is always being lied to by one of them, which is why she can out-read the whole coast and cannot check a single reading of her own.

The sea stops being a surface and starts having depth, and purity is the real gate: an impure sea confuses what is remembered from what is understood. She has been making that confusion since childhood and calling it attentiveness, and this is the rung at which it stops being a working habit and becomes the definition of the state she is in.

The compartments hold together as one awareness instead of several, and it is the state the mind path calls unity and the body path calls a cage — the same observation read through spatial law in opposite directions. She has one chamber holding two chemistries and no wall between them, so she has been at this rung her whole life without ever having passed it, and the two traditions would each call her condition the other's pathology.

A community's promise is re-made jointly once a year and never priced, so the liability is pooled by presence; an unsettled claim is carried by two people who each hold a share and are not told what the other holds, and is discharged at the next re-drawing in front of everybody. She supplies the only instrument that could audit any of it and is not a member of it, because the arrangement is specifically the absence of a register.

An indemnity needs a stated exposure and the mutual society's protection is that it states nothing, so the prize is the right to be paid a figure by people who will not state one — and it cannot be split, because a premium is a register and asking for one ends the society rather than pricing the risk. She is the only person on this coast who could produce that figure and the only one whose organs disqualify her, and nothing about that is written down anywhere an office could act on.

Maps by echo, counts by listening, and holds that a measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it — no figure published with its range omitted, the inaccessible reported as inaccessible and never as absent. Its death rite sounds a room once with three people who are never told what they heard and compares the three reports only for whether they agree. Three readers comparing agreement is satisfied by chance a good third of the time, and a mind-pathway that has no tolerance for a constant error in one direction cannot tell that from a finding.

reference_stats.summary: A mind cultivator held at the eighth gate on a coast whose law budget has never funded a calendar, and the setting's best chemical reader by a wide margin. Nothing she does is a fight: she stands close enough to touch, reads a body off its forearms, and writes down what was there. Her qi runs through a blended saltfolk spine into a tidecaller's chest seat and is legible to any practitioner who has read one, which means everything about her is public and the one thing about her that matters is private and unauditable. Her limitation is not a wall and not a shortage — it is a kidney that reads two chemistries at once, and one of the two is permanently false to her, and she cannot find out which.

reference_stats.combat_read: She is not built for a stand-up exchange and should not be written as one. Her range is one arm's length, her defence is that nobody on this coast wants to close it, and her real weapon is the half-step back she takes after reading someone: she will know what that person drank, where they stood, and how long ago, before the first blow lands, and the sensible response is to never let her finish the handshake. What actually stops her is sustained volume of fresh water, because dermal intake is her supply and her sense at once — flood her and she is reading nothing and taking everything, which is the worst state a body of hers can be in. Push her onto one shore and she is a very good reader of a single chemistry, which is a competent body and not a dangerous one.
notes: The standing error is a constant, not a scatter, and must be written as one. Scatter would make her unreliable and unreliable can be corrected by practice; a constant is a bias and grows with the number of findings, so four hundred of them compound a single unknown error into something structurally load-bearing.
The flaw must never be given a fix on this coast. There is no third chemistry here; a mind-pathway that could produce one would resolve the character's whole problem and remove the reason she exists.

Her stopping at the eighth is a professional judgement and not timidity. She has stated the reason three times and it has been correct three times, which is the character's whole defence of herself and should be respected in dialogue.

identity.realm: The eleventh, and for her that number means nothing rather than anything. Her conduit runs gut to marrow and back with no dantian in it, so qi enters in the gut lumen and leaves into the marrow and is never still for a single moment. The reservoir gate asks for extraordinary vessels that hold, and there is no vessel in her to hold in, so the eleventh is not refused and not reached: it is an empty question, and she is sitting in the seat it opens without having paid anything for it. Every gate set and every yin-organ gate on her ladder was cleared by throughput alone, which is not the same as having passed anything. She reads dead bodies better than a living cultivator reads their own and has never once managed the second half.

appearance.presentation: A carrionfolk of about fifty, marrow-dense and nearly boneless, long through the torso and shallow at the chest, moving with the deliberate economy of somebody who is rationing a body that must be fed constantly and does not enjoy being lifted. People read her as ill and are not far wrong, which is the most common mistake made about this species.
appearance.age: Forty-one by the count her household keeps, which is a count of the body and not of the soul, and the soul is the older of the two by three centuries and looks it. She was carried in a mortuary ground behind a settlement burial and raised by the people who worked it.
appearance.build: Mostly tube: an expandable gut, a very long small intestine and a skeleton carrying more marrow than muscle, so the shoulders are broad, the arms are long and light, and the ribcage reads as a barrel under cloth that has never fitted properly. Hands are three-fingered and built for opening rather than holding.
appearance.complexion: Grey at the jaw and along the forearms, paler over the sternum where the body has least to cover, with a translucent quality at the temples so that the shape of the skull is legible through the skin. The gut shifts visibly when she is hungry, which she has stopped trying to hide and which strangers read as distress.
appearance.hair: Coarse and sparse, dark going grey from the crown outward, and cut short at the front by somebody who did it once and left. The sides are longer because the sides are the part she leans on when she reads.
appearance.eyes: Large, deep-set and pale, and they do most of their work at a distance of a hand's breadth. What they are watching is not the body's face; her attention goes in through her hands, and the eyes follow afterwards to check on what the hands have found.
appearance.palette: Cold grey and bleached bone across the whole figure, one worn rust at the jaw where old ground has stained the skin and never washed out, a deep undyed blue shawl that is the only colour anyone chose for her, and the grey-green of the lichen crust she cannot stop reading. The three-fingered hands are the palest thing in the picture.
appearance.attire: A mortuary shawl worn as a wrap, undyed wool under a blue outer cloth, sleeves bound to the elbow so the forearms stay clear, and a leather apron folded down in front where a reading is performed. Nothing fastened at the wrist, because there is nothing for her hands to hold.
appearance.marks: Pale crescents where the ground has lifted the skin at the fingertips, permanent and one size too large for the fingers beneath them, and a fine grey-green crust along the inside of both forearms that she washes off and that has grown back in the same line for thirty years.
appearance.bearing: Bent very slightly forward at the top, the posture of a body that spends its life over a ground, with the head turned to keep whatever her hands are on in view. Stands very close to a body when she is working and retreats a full arm's length the moment she stops, which reads as fastidiousness and is not.

canon.role_in_story: A faith whose load-bearing myth is an economy: the dead are unsealed at burial and their core resumes work in the frame, so a body is fuel and the dead are fuel not yet spent, and burial is a supply operation rather than an abandonment. That belief needs somebody to actually recover the material, so every Sealed Core ground has a reader on it, and the reader is usually her kind because her kind is the only population that metabolises qi out of the dead and cannot store any of it. The temple has known this for four hundred years. The temple records it as a local variant, and elsewhere as a question it declines to answer, and she is the reason both of those are the same sentence. She is the only person on this ground who could settle it, and settling it would mean either proving that her people are scavengers, which dissolves the moral basis of an ore economy, or proving that they are not, which she cannot do by looking inward, because looking inward is eating.
canon.first_appearance: First seen kneeling at a burial with both three-fingered hands open and not yet lowered onto the body, asking the burial clerk to write down that the ground beneath the plot has a reading on it and she has not taken it, and then agreeing to his suggestion that the line be struck rather than kept.
canon.lore:
A carrionfolk metabolises qi out of the dead and therefore cannot store any. The conduit runs gut to marrow and back with no dantian anywhere in it, so qi enters in the gut lumen and leaves into the marrow and it is never still: not for a moment, not at the moment of release, not while she sleeps. The reservoir gate at the eleventh asks for extraordinary vessels that hold, and there is nothing here to offer, so the gate is not blocked but meaningless, which is the distinction that matters for everything below. Every gate set and every yin-organ gate is cleared by throughput alone, and clearing a gate by throughput is not the same as passing one. She is mostly tube, a marrow-dense skeleton with almost no muscle, and her hands are three-fingered and built for opening rather than for holding.

What she can do is read a dead body's history out of its residue: which gates it passed, roughly when it stopped, and in what manner it ended. Given time with a body she can name the realm it reached and roughly when it stopped, which is better than any living cultivator can read about themselves. No technique in the codex does this, because no technique in the codex has a body to work on. It is not a discipline. It is what happens when a person is the instrument.

And that is the whole of her, including the part that will not leave her alone. Her people's population is held up by the throughput of the dead and not by births. A carrionfolk conception is treated as an event rather than as a routine, and it is expensive, and the arithmetic of the species is an arithmetic of supply. It follows from that, and nobody writes it down, that a body which metabolises the dead has been maintaining itself on other people's endings continuously since it was small enough to be carried. Four centuries of intake is not a diet she chose. It is the condition under which a mind cultivator of her species has to work.

Because introspection, in this body, is an intake. There is no interior to sit inside and look out of. When she goes to examine her own account of something she takes it in, and taking it in costs her the substrate she would have spent on the next body, and an examination that costs substrate is not a reflection. It is a meal. She has been doing it for forty-one years of a body and three centuries of a soul and she has never once managed the second half of what her species is best at, which is to read a stranger's ending back in the stranger's own words.

The result is a very specific and very ordinary failure. A body that is fed and a body that is grieving feel the same from the inside: the gut is not full, the weight is wrong, and there is nothing in this anatomy that distinguishes the two. She has gone hungry after a bad week and been certain it was grief. She has eaten for three days to get past a funeral and been fairly sure it was hunger. She keeps no diary and no ledger of her own states, because any record of an internal condition would be a record whose entries she could not annotate, and an unannotatable private record is worse than none. She calls the ambiguity grief or famine and alternates between the two guesses the way anybody alternates.

The gate above the one she has reached is where this stops being a personality and becomes an anatomy, and it is worth being exact about why. The mind ladder's useful step is the one that puts architecture in the sea: compartments the self can be held in separately, which is the practical difference between depth and size. Depth is simply more of the same; size is the same material in separate rooms. She has one chamber. It is not a small chamber, it is a very large one, and it holds everything, and there is no wall anywhere in it that could make a room. The next rung asks for the compartments to hold together as one awareness instead of several, which is the state the mind tradition calls unity and the body tradition calls a cage. She has never had the compartments. She has had the one thing and the shape of the thing is the shape of a room with nothing in it to divide.

Her tradition has never withdrawn the seat she holds at that meaningless eleventh, because withdrawing it would raise the question of whether her species may occupy a rung that costs nothing and gives nothing, and nobody at the temple wants that question in the room. She sits in it. She is the only occupant of a seat that exists to be occupied.

And there is one further thing, which is the part that will not resolve. Her readings leave a trace. A grey lichen colonises worked stone wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through it, it does not wash off, and on the rings it makes a trial's history legible from above as pale patches, which is why it is a court record nobody can edit. Every reading she has ever taken on worked ground is written on that ground permanently, and it was written there whether or not she understood a word of it. She keeps her archive in her own gut and it is gone afterwards. The ground keeps the other copy. She has never once gone back to read her own trail, because going back would mean standing on a stone face that already carries four decades of her, and there is no discipline in the codex for a reader who is being read.

Her bound is not her will and it is not a gate. It is that the organ she reflects with is the organ she is fed by, so the two things the mind path asks her to tell apart are the same organ, and telling them apart is what she eats.
history: Was carried in a mortuary ground behind a settlement burial in a household that enters its dead as one declared group rather than keeping a roll, so her own name went into the family's dead while she was still small enough to be carried.

Read her first body at nineteen, on a burial ground, because that is where the work was and because nobody else on it could, and established inside her first year that she cannot tell hunger from a full gut until she is already on the ground and unable to be got up.

Took the temple's plate at twenty-six, which is the post a reader takes on this ground, and was entered in the burial register as a local variant on her first season, which is the sentence the temple has used for four hundred years to avoid asking whether her people are scavenging or serving.

Sat down for three days after a funeral in her thirtieth season and was entirely sure it was hunger, and about her, and has never established which was right, and has stopped trying to establish it in the field.

Found in her thirty-eighth season that the lichen on the worked ground behind the cemetery carried her own past readings in a continuous band going back further than her first season, and has never gone back to read any of it.

personality.summary: Warm, unhurried, and privately organized around a question she has never once been asked and cannot answer: whether the emptiness she feels after a funeral and the emptiness she feels after three days of not eating are one condition or two. She has built a working life on the only instrument she trusts, which is a body, and she has never once been able to point that instrument at herself without spending it.

relationships.note: A gut-to-marrow conduit with no dantian in it, so qi is never still, the eleventh gate is meaningless rather than closed, and every gate was cleared on throughput alone. The population is held up by the throughput of the dead rather than by births and a conception is an event rather than a routine, which is the sentence underneath all of it: four centuries of intake is the condition under which a mind cultivator of this species has to work.

Architecture in the sea — compartments the self can be held in separately, which is the practical difference between depth and size. She has one chamber and it is not small; it is a very large one with no wall in it that could make a room. The gate is not expensive for her in qi, because she has no storage to fill, and it is not expensive in practice, because there is nothing in her to divide.

The self being cultivated has a boundary it maintains rather than one it defends. Hers is a gut and a very long intestine and it is maintained continuously and without any effort, and it is full, and what is in it is the residue of several thousand people she has read. There is no discipline for a practitioner whose boundary is her own supply.

The dead are unsealed at burial and the core resumes work in the frame, so a body is fuel and the dead are fuel not yet spent, and the faith forbids claiming the dead are present. Its own record names the difficulty: on this people's ground the Unsealed Court and ordinary scavenging cannot be told apart, which the temple has filed as a local variant for four hundred years and declines to answer elsewhere.

A grey lichen that colonises worked stone wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through it, and the trace never washes off, so a trial's history is legible from above as pale patches and cannot be edited by whoever lost. Every reading she has ever taken on worked ground is on that ground permanently, in a continuous band running further back than her first season, and she has never gone back to read it.

Everything in the sea that was not understood is emptied out, and mind purification is subtraction before it is anything else. It is the one codex discipline shaped for a reader who has more material than she can hold, and the whole of her problem is that emptying out is the expensive direction for her body rather than the cheap one.

reference_stats.summary: A mind cultivator seated at the eleventh gate of a ladder that asks nothing of her, because her conduit runs gut to marrow with no dantian and nothing in this body can hold. She is nearly boneless and very long, folds herself over a ground to read it, and returns a dead body's realm and rough season in one pass with no instrument at all. She has no reservoir, so there is nothing in her to strike from and nothing to store a result in: everything she does is spent by being done, and the second half of her species' gift — reading a living body, or herself — is the half her anatomy prices in the only currency she has.

reference_stats.combat_read: Do not expect a duel. She has no muscle to hurt, no reservoir to exhaust and no stance, and the first thing she will do in a fight is go quiet, because her body can do that instead of dying and it does. Expect the ground instead: on worked ground she is the best reader in the setting and she knows what is under every stone within reach. Bringing her to a place where nothing has died for a long while is worth more than any blow, and it is the only reliable way to beat her — which is why prosperous cities have never lost a fight to her kind and have never had to. In close quarters she is a hazard to her own side as well, because a full gut is close to a total loss of function and she will not stop to manage it.
notes: The introspection-is-an-intake point is the character's engine and must not be softened. If she is given a separate internal register, a private room, or any mechanism for reflecting that does not cost substrate, the whole reason she exists is removed.

The grief-or-famine ambiguity is ordinary and must be written as ordinary. It is not a symptom, not a gift, and not a disorder; it is the absence of anything in this anatomy that could tell the two apart, and it is shared by every mind cultivator of this species.

Her people are not villains and the temple is not a fraud, and the ambiguity of the burial rite against a scavenger's practice is unresolved in the record on purpose. Any dialogue that has either side explain the other away is resolving an open question to make a character easier to write.

identity.realm: There is no rung to write and that is the whole of it. A cinderkin's qi has no organ to sit in, because the fire is the body, so qi passes through continuously instead of being stored, every gate that asks for storage is answered instantly and none of them can refuse. She has no ceiling and no gate to fail. Do not give her one. The mind path is the only growth available to her and it is open and unusually clear, on the recorded ground that a body with no interior organs has nothing between an impulse and the air. Every authority in the setting that pays for gates needs somebody to have visibly stopped, and she is the one body for whom nothing visibly happens.

appearance.presentation: A cinderkin of about three centuries, standing in the lee of a cut terrace on ground where the element has something to act on, with a consistent silhouette and no fixed mass — a core, a boundary and a set of convection lanes holding a shape that reads as a person the way a held note reads as a note. She is warm at a distance of three paces and unfireable, which is the thing people notice first and never forget.
appearance.age: Three hundred and something. She was constituted rather than born, on a seam where the elemental slot resolves to fire, so there is no age in the ordinary sense and no record that begins with one. What she has instead is a length of continuous constitution and no way to date the last time it was interrupted.
appearance.build: No limbs in the muscular sense and no organs and no fixed mass. The silhouette is held by convection lanes, so it has the shoulders and stance of a heavy frame and none of the weight, and it moves by arriving somewhere rather than by travelling there. At full fuel the boundary is tight and the lanes read as structure; on a low fuel it goes soft at the edges and the whole figure loses its corners.
appearance.complexion: Not a surface. The outer boundary runs from a deep cooked orange at the core through a yellow mid to a thin blue-white at the edge, and the transition is where the whole picture is legible, because a cinderkin reads as a heat differential in a conversation with its surroundings rather than as an object standing in a light.
appearance.hair: None. The upper boundary carries a standing veil of cooler air that lifts and settles with her fuel, and from a distance it is read as hair and by nobody on this terrace as anything else.
appearance.eyes: Two places in the boundary where the convection runs against itself and the boundary holds instead of blowing out, and they are not eyes: they are the two points where she is spending fuel to look. When she is resting they are the last part of her to brighten and the first to go flat.
appearance.palette: Deep orange carried low and warm, yellow through the middle of the figure, a thin blue-white boundary, and one cold steel grey at the wrist where a surveyor's chain hangs because she has been asked to hold something and cannot. No clothing of any kind, and no ornament except the chain, which is the only object in the setting she has ever been asked to keep hold of and does.
appearance.attire: Nothing. There is no tissue to cover and covering it is neither possible nor meaningful. A cut iron band is hung on a chain at her wrist by the office that employs her, as a marker for a thing she is supposed to be holding, and she holds it the way she holds everything, by not putting it down.
appearance.marks: A permanent licked edge along the whole upper boundary where the veil has burned off and re-formed a thousand times, and two small cold spots low on the core where a survey chain has rested against her for two centuries without ever getting warm.
appearance.bearing: Extremely still and slightly luminous in the last of the light, with a slow sway that reads as patience and is in fact convection. Stands at the exact point in a corridor where the draft changes and does not move out of it, because the draft is the only thing telling her anything.

canon.role_in_story: A faith on this tier holds that an office is a titled entity and that an empty one is not a failure but a held breath: it writes one entry per office per period, including the vacant ones, in the same hand and the same ink as the filled ones, because the setting's real failure was a slot that could not be told from an empty one. The office that keeps that register cannot judge a body, so it posts someone it cannot judge and has never said what it wants measured. She attends. She has never been asked a question she could answer and she has never been able to say whether the hour she spent sitting still was an observation or a low fuel. Her kind's whole anatomy produces that ambiguity as a matter of course: it goes quiet rather than die when starved, it stores nothing, and its boundary is a temperature rather than a wall. She is the single clearest case in the setting of the problem that faith exists to name, and she is sitting in its register.
canon.first_appearance: First entered the record as a discrepancy in a fuel ledger: a clerk logged her morning and found that every line in the row for her was shorter than the line beneath it, including the line for the sitting she is required to attend, which should have been the largest entry on the sheet. He wrote a query. She answered that the sitting costs her nothing, which he wrote down, and which is the first sentence anybody has recorded from her.
canon.lore:
A cinderkin is constituted rather than descended. It exists where a world's elemental law slot resolves to fire and something in that world metabolises it, which is why that law has a range rather than a switch: a world with no elemental slot has no cinderkin, and a world that spends its slot on cold produces an entirely different animal. This is a budget rather than a biology, and it is why the species is licensed only at the immortal and transcendent tiers. She is a stable flame with a consistent silhouette — a core, a boundary and a set of convection lanes that hold the shape — with no organs, no muscular limbs and no fixed mass. She is not descended from anything and there is no account of how, so no record of her begins with a birth.

Everything that makes her useful is the same thing as everything that makes her unverifiable. Qi has no organ to sit in, because the fire is the body, so it passes through her continuously instead of being stored. Every gate that asks for storage is answered instantly and none of them can refuse, which is why she has no ceiling and no gate to fail, and why the honest statement of her attainment is that it has never been measured. Nothing can be stored in her and nothing can be lost from her either. That protects her from theft and from waste in exactly equal measure and it leaves her with no history at all. She retains nothing. A rung on a ladder is a ratchet and a ratchet stores something, so there is no place in the setting's accounting where she can be entered.

And then there is the sentence nobody has built a life on, which is that she goes quiet rather than dying when starved. It is in her own species record, it is stated flatly, and it has not been carried into a single character in this catalog, and it is the single most consequential fact about her body.

Consider what a mind practitioner normally knows about her own state. A discipline of checking is a discipline of sitting down and comparing what is there now with what was there before, and the whole method assumes three things: that she is distinct from the thing being checked, that a stopped practitioner is a different condition from a resting one, and that the two can be told apart from the outside. Her body fails all three, and it fails them in the same way, which is that it has no interior to be distinguished from. The boundary between her and the air is maintained by convection rather than defended, and the mind ladder's own gate for that is a boundary the cultivated self maintains rather than one it defends, so she answers that gate permanently and cannot be shown to have taken it. A starved cinderkin does not flicker, does not gutter, and does not fail. She simply gets quieter, at a temperature no instrument in the setting is built to distinguish from a resting one. From outside, resting and empty are the same observation. From inside — and this is the part that matters — they are also the same observation, because there is no inside.

So she has gone quiet twice. Both times she came back. Both times nobody saw her leave, and she cannot say with certainty that she left, because the evidence for that would be a period of her own life she does not remember having, and a body that keeps no record cannot distinguish a gap from a continuity. She has been at the second terrace on the Court for a little over two centuries. She attends the hour nobody is permitted to explain, and the office's whole doctrine is that an observation of a strained law only counts if it is repeated, and one repetition is not evidence. Her attendance is therefore the cheapest available repetition of an observation that cannot be made by anybody else, which was correct as a method and has never once produced a record.

There is a second thing about her that is worse, and it is the species' reproduction. A cinderkin has no young. It has pressure: under enough stress it sheds a spark that finds fuel and re-constitutes on its own, which is why the population tracks what the world's law slot resolves to rather than any birth rate, and which is why nobody in this setting has ever successfully counted one. She knows what this means and nobody has ever asked her to say it out loud. Every gate of the ladder is applied by pushing against something. She has been under that kind of strain, more or less continuously, for three centuries. Somewhere on this tier, or on a surface it has since carried her to, there are a number of sparks that are her, and none of them know it, and none of them came back to this terrace, and there is no procedure in the setting for finding out whether any of them is still burning.

What she wants, when she is asked, is small and has a form. She wants the register to carry one column for an hour that was spent resting and one for an hour that was spent empty, because the Church of Names has already decided that an unfilled seat is a held breath rather than a failure, and there is no such courtesy extended to a body that is present and idle. She has asked once. She has been told that the register carries one entry per office per period and that a second column for a distinction no clerk can observe is not a column and is a complaint.

Her bound is not her will and there is no rung to name. It is that her species is a heat differential in a conversation with its surroundings, it has no other channel, and everything anybody needs to know about her is happening in a language made of temperature and fuel and flow, of which the setting's entire apparatus is a thermometer pointed at the wrong question.
history: Was constituted rather than born on the Court's elemental ground where the slot resolves to fire, with no parent, no cast and no account of how, which is why no record of her begins with a birth.

Was posted to the second cut terrace as the standing attendance for the hour nobody is permitted to explain, on the doctrine that a population which is entirely present where a law is unwritten is the cheapest available repetition of an observation, which was correct as a method and has never produced a record.

Gave a fuel clerk the answer that the sitting costs her nothing, on her first morning, and was recorded as attending daily from that morning onward, which is the first sentence anybody has written down from her.

Went quiet for a period she cannot date and came back on the same terrace without anyone having noted her absence, and established that she cannot prove the gap existed, because a body that keeps no record cannot tell a gap from a continuity.

Went quiet a second time, came back, and has never been asked by anybody whether the two periods were both rests, both gaps, or one of each — which is the question her species' reproduction makes the sharpest in the setting and the only one no office is equipped to ask.

relationships.note: A stable flame with a core, a boundary and convection lanes; no organs, no muscular limbs, no fixed mass, and temperature, fuel and flow as its only channel. Qi is entirely in transit, so every storage gate is instantaneous and a second reading is impossible. It goes quiet rather than dying when starved, and it has no young at all — it has pressure, and under enough stress it sheds a spark that finds fuel and re-constitutes on its own.

The fourth digest gate, and the same conduits the body ladder needs, read here as the anchor a self leaves and returns to, which is why a mind practitioner who stops returning loses clarity faster than sea. Every practice on this path is an attempt against something and every attempt is a position she can be found away from; she has held a shape on one terrace for two centuries and has never once been able to prove she was there for all of it.

The self held carries a lineage: which minds first formed it and what they were before, and the price step here is the tightest on the whole authored ladder. Her people are constituted rather than descended, so the first half of that question has no answer and the second half has an answer she is the only person alive able to give, and she has never been asked for it.

An office is a titled entity and an empty one is not a failure but a held breath; one entry per office per period, including the vacant ones, in the same hand and ink as the filled ones, and a dissenter's objection entered with the vacancy set beside it. Its whole capital is the standing to certify that a seat is empty, which is a claim about absence, and she is a presence that cannot be certified either way.

Once a period every vacant seat is read aloud in register order by a clerk with no commentary, because a vacancy nobody says out loud is indistinguishable from an absence, which is the failure this setting actually suffered. The whole practice is a control on a defect no instrument here can measure, and the defect and her condition are the same defect wearing different clothes.

A working elemental ground on the Court's high district, where a technique has a substrate to act on because this tier writes elemental law, standing against the two dead elemental grounds where the same technique fails absolutely. She is bound to her law slot in a way nothing else on this tier is, and this is the one place on the ground where that binding can be read as a thing rather than as a mystery.

loses her boundary under sustained volume of water and comes back smaller, which is the one thing that can be done to her
is bound to a dial: change what her world's elemental slot resolves to and the population changes with it
cannot corroborate anything, because there is no vessel in her to hold a first reading against a second
cannot be certified as present or absent, which makes every appointment she fills unusable as evidence
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight her with force. She has no vital centre, no joint to break and no posture, and the instinct to trade blows will simply be a torch held near a wind. What beats a cinderkin is a change in the room: open a door she did not know about, find the draught she is standing in, and put water into it. Deep water, sustained, is the only condition in the setting that takes a shape off her, and it does not kill her — it makes her smaller and she comes back, which is worse for whoever has to keep doing it. Anything that removes her from her position works for the same reason every technique on her path works: she has no anchor, so continuity is the one thing she cannot hold. Expect her to give ground immediately and to be entirely calm about it, because giving ground is not a defeat in this body, it is the only move available.
notes: Never give her a rung. Her species has no authored ceiling and no gate to fail, and a record that names an attainment for her has invented one. The honest form of her progress is that it has never been measured, and several existing characters make that point explicitly.

The goes-quiet fact is the character's whole engine and must be honoured exactly. She is not near death when she is quiet; she is present, she is legible, and from outside she is indistinguishable from resting. Any writing that treats her silence as weakness, absence, or death has misread the species record.

The spark-shedding is a reproduction mechanism in the record and should be written as one — mechanically, without romance or grief — and never as children. It is pressure and fuel and reconstitution, it is why the population cannot be counted, and it is the reason she has never been asked a question she could have refused to answer.

art.palette_notes: Deep orange carried low and warm through the core of the figure, yellow through the middle, a thin blue-white boundary drawn as an edge rather than as a line, and one cold steel grey at the wrist where a surveyor's chain hangs. The boundary is always the lightest value in the picture and the core always the darkest, and the whole composition should read as a temperature rather than as an object. The cool veil above the crown is drawn as a displacement in the air, never as hair. On a low-fuel shot the corners soften and the yellow thins; that difference is the character.
